content:
**Summary:**

- **Running time depends on input size:** Sorting more elements (e.g., 6×10⁹ vs. 6) takes longer, so running time is analyzed as a function of input size.
- **Focus on upper bounds:** We typically want to know the maximum time an algorithm could take, not the minimum.
- **Why upper bounds matter:** They provide a guarantee to users (e.g., "won't run more than 3 seconds" is useful for real-time applications), whereas a lower bound ("at least 3 seconds") gives no assurance about worst-case performance.
